transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cara Vakulman.
President Trump is in Shenzhen, China, holding meetings with other world leaders on the sidelines
of an economic summit.
His most anticipated meeting will come later.
Trump is expected to hold a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian
President Vladimir Putin.
It's not clear what the three will focus on.
Trump has wanted to discuss denuclearization.
Putin has wanted to talk about the war in Ukraine, and Xi is interested in trade, especially
since U.S. exports of key computer chips for AI have installed.
But before that trilateral meeting happens, Trump may hold another conversation.
NPR has learned from White House officials, not authorized to speak on the record, Trump
and Putin have their own meeting planned on their expected agenda.
Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen is testifying before a House committee.
Lawmakers are expected to ask him about last week's airline ground stop.
The Trump administration says it's looking at infrastructure.
Dave Hinchman is the director of information technology and cybersecurity at the Government
Accountability Office.
He says some government systems are just old.
The government spends at least $100 billion on information technology every year.
And about 80% of that is to operate and maintain existing technology, with the remaining 20%
being used to develop new technology.
And within that operations and maintenance budget are these what we call legacy IT systems
that can really pose significant challenges, and that could be because of outdated computer
programming language, unsupported hardware, software or even known cyber vulnerabilities
that need to be attended to.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
House Democrats have nominated New York Democrat Hakeem Jeffries as their leader for the next
Congress.
He is widely expected to become the next speaker of the House.
Meanwhile, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee is previewing his investigations
that are expected next January.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt reports the targets include over a dozen allies and family members of
President Trump.
Robert Garcia, who is expected to be the next chair of the House Oversight Committee, sent
a dozen document preservation letters, a signal of investigations to come.
The California Democrats' targets fall into four broad categories, Trump family corruption,
corporate corruption, DHS misconduct and the White House Epstein cover-up.
States include the President's sons and son-in-law, former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, White House
Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Vice President J.D. Vance.
The Trump administration has previously rejected accusations of misconduct.
Barbara Sprunt and PR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
The Associated Press has called the outstanding Senate race in Alaska for Democratic challenger
Mary Peltola.
She defeated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan with slightly more than 50 percent of the vote.
Peltola released a video statement thanking supporters and promising to get to work immediately.
We need to fight corruption and corporate greed.
We need to bring prices down.
We need to lower fuel costs and build new homes.
And we need to ensure that Alaskans are served by your elected senators.
There are a handful of House races that the AP has not yet called.
That includes Alaska's lone House race.
Republican incumbent Nick Begich currently leans.
In Britain, the Cambridge dictionary has come out with its Word of the Year.
Vicky Barker has more from London.
Call it a defiant shaking of the lexicographical fist at ever more powerful invisible forces.
The Cambridge dictionary's Word of the Year for 2026 is human, defining the word as "having
the qualities, faults and feelings that people have as opposed to God's animals or machines."
Cambridge is not above using those machines itself, including an AI tool on its website.
Tech-adjacent words were among the new additions this year, including "look-smaxing" and
"ora-farming," which it defines as "the activity of doing things with the intention
of showing a personality that people admire and think is attractive and interesting."
For NPR News, I'm Vicky Barker in London.
And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump in Shenzhen, China, holding summit meetings with world leaders on economic summit sidelines
Trump expected to hold trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, agenda unclear
Trump and Putin reportedly plan their own separate meeting before the trilateral, per White House officials
Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullin testifies before House committee on last week's airline ground stop
GAO's Dave Hinchman says aging legacy government IT systems pose major challenges and cybersecurity risks
Hakeem Jeffries nominated by House Democrats as leader, widely expected to become next House speaker
Robert Garcia previews House Oversight Democrats' investigations into Trump family, DHS, and White House Epstein handling
Mary Peltola defeats Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, AP calls it for Democrat
Nick Begich leads in Alaska's lone House race, which AP has not yet called
Cambridge Dictionary names 'human' its 2026 Word of the Year, adds tech-related terms like 'look-smaxing'
